questions.q: Why do both product-catalog and checkout run as Kubernetes Deployments rather than StatefulSets?
options: StatefulSets are deprecated
They are stateless — all persistent state lives in Postgres Flexible Server outside the cluster
Deployments are required for all Node.js and Python apps
StatefulSets cannot be used with Helm
questions.explain: Since neither service stores state locally, they can be freely killed and rescheduled as interchangeable replicas, which is exactly what a Deployment is designed for; a StatefulSet would be unnecessary complexity.

questions.q: What problem does Terraform remote state with blob-lease locking solve?
options: It makes Terraform run faster
It prevents two concurrent terraform apply runs from racing against the same state and corrupting it
It replaces the need for version control
It automatically fixes configuration syntax errors
questions.explain: Locking ensures that when one apply is in progress, a second apply is blocked with a clear error instead of racing against the same state file.

questions.q: In the Northbridge state-collision story, what actually happened when two engineers ran terraform apply at the same time?
options: The state file was silently corrupted
The second apply was blocked with a 'state is locked' error until the first completed
Both applies succeeded and overwrote each other's changes
Azure automatically merged the two changes
questions.explain: Because the backend used blob-lease locking, the second apply was cleanly blocked rather than allowed to race, demonstrating exactly why remote state with locking matters.

questions.q: Roughly how does a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler compute its desired replica count?
options: It always doubles the current replica count
Current replicas multiplied by the ratio of current metric to target metric, clamped between min and max
It picks a random number within the configured range
It only reacts to memory usage, never CPU
questions.explain: The HPA controller computes desired replicas proportionally based on how far current utilization is from the target, within the configured min/max bounds.

questions.q: Why does checkout's HPA use a wider range (3-15 pods) than product-catalog's (2-8 pods)?
options: It was copy-pasted from a template without consideration
Checkout experiences spikier flash-sale load and needs more headroom to scale
Checkout uses a different programming language
Wider ranges are always better regardless of traffic shape
questions.explain: HPA ranges should reflect the real shape of a service's traffic; checkout's spiky flash-sale load justifies a wider scaling range than product-catalog's steadier traffic.
